channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Carry appeal capped by Oil risk – BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu notes that India’s central bank (RBI) has stepped in to support the Indian Rupee (INR) as rising energy costs threaten external balances and FX volatility. iFlow shows INR is currently underheld versus earlier in the year.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: keeps the Bullish bias intact above 101.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) shows moderate losses on Wednesday but has retraced most of the decline seen during the Asian trading session.

item.title: Gold hits two-week high as traders weigh Middle East risks, Fed outlook
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) climbs to a two-week high on Wednesday as bargain hunters step in near the $4,000 mark, while traders weigh Middle East risks and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy outlook.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Hawkish BoJ signals versus Fed risk – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses Japanese Yen (JPY) prospects, focusing on USD/JPY. Foley highlight that intervention by the Ministry of Finance (MoF) alone is unlikely to change the pair’s direction without improved Japanese fundamentals.

item.title: British Pound: Heavy trade as BoE seen adjusting – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the British Pound (GBP) remains heavy versus the US Dollar (USD) and Euro (EUR) after a mixed United Kingdom (UK) June Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, with headline inflation cooling but core and services measures still sticky.

item.title: Silver price edges higher as geopolitical tensions offset inflation concerns
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $59.35 at the time of writing on Wednesday, up 0.94% on the day, as persistent safe-haven demand offsets the negative impact of rising inflation expectations.

item.title: Euro: Drifting toward ECB test – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING notes EUR/USD has held up relatively well despite energy price gains and wider natural gas prices.

item.title: Euro holds near five-week highs against Yen despite BoJ tightening rumours
item.description: The Euro (EUR) reversed earlier gains against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Wednesday, following hawkish comments by Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) policymakers. The pair, however, remains a few pips below 186.00 at the time of writing, with the five-week high of 186.19 at a short distance.

item.title: World Bank warns of risks of global slowdown, renewed inflation
item.description: The World Bank warned that the global economy is only "a few months" away from a worst-case scenario in which global growth slows to 1.3% while inflation rises to 4.5%, according to comments by Chief Economist Indermit Gill reported by Reuters.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls back as oil prices rally further
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after a slight relief the previous day. The USD/INR pair rises to near 96.53 as a fresh surge in oil prices due to intensifying fears of further global energy supply disruptions has weakened the Indian currency.

item.title: United States Sec. of State Rubio: Iran is in a lot of trouble
item.description: Following his meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Manila on Wednesday, United States (US) Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that “Iran is in a lot of trouble.”

item.title: US Dollar: Trade tariffs to reshape FX volatility – MUFG
item.description: Derek Halpenny at MUFG explains that US trade tariff uncertainty is set to re-emerge as Section 122 measures expire and are replaced by more targeted Section 301 actions.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD holds gains above $4,100 undaunted by risk-off markets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends gains for the fourth consecutive day on Wednesday, standing comfortably above $4,100, unfazed by the risk-off market amid rising tensions in Iran and higher Oil prices.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Technical outlook weakens against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight USD/JPY trading in breakout territory above 163 for the first time in nearly four decades, with support around 162.20 and resistance near 164.40.

item.title: Swiss Franc edges higher as US-Iran tensions, higher Swiss yields sustain support
item.description: USD/CHF trades around 0.8120 at the time of writing on Wednesday, down a modest 0.09% on the day, but remains supported by a strong risk-off environment that favors the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: UK inflation cools and fiscal concerns grow: Why the British Pound is surrendering recent gains
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is facing renewed downward pressure across major currency pairs, forfeiting its recent gains as market participants digest a combination of cooling domestic inflation and growing fiscal uncertainty surrounding Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s economic agenda.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $59.50 per troy ounce, up 1.19% from the $58.80 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens as global risk aversion overshadows hawkish RBNZ outlook
item.description: NZD/USD extends its losing streak for the fifth successive day, trading around 0.5810 during the European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Dovish tilt keeps easing alive – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reports that Hungary’s central bank Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) cut its base rate to 5.75%, in line with expectations, and maintained its summer easing narrative.

item.title: British Pound sticks to post-UK inflation losses as faster BoJ rate hike bets lift JPY
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross attracts some intraday sellers on Wednesday and slides below the 218.00 mark during the first half of the European session. Spot prices remain, however, confined within the previous day's broader range amid the supportive fundamental backdrop.

item.title: Oil: Supply risks support Brent valuations – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight growing Oil supply disruptions across the Middle East and Black Sea. They note risks to Saudi crude exports via the Red Sea, renewed Persian Gulf tensions, and halted Kazakhstan flows through Russia’s CPC terminal.

item.title: Australian Dollar weakens as global energy supply disrupts further
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) underperforms its major currency peers, trading marginally down at around 0.7000 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Remains below 50-day EMA near the confluence of 1.3400
item.description: GBP/USD remains steady after four days of losses, trading around 1.3370 during the European hours on Wednesday. The pair is holding a mildly bearish near‑term bias as spot remains capped beneath the 50‑day and nine-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Australian Dollar: 0.6970 support keeps upside intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report AUD/USD has eased after testing above 0.7020, with intraday price action now seen consolidating between 0.6985 and 0.7020.

item.title: Euro remains stuck near 1.1400 amid rising tensions in Iran, higher Oil prices
item.description: The Euro’s (EUR) modest upside attempt against the US Dollar (USD) witnessed during Wednesday’s Asian session has been short-lived. The EUR/USD pair was capped below 1.1420, before pulling back to levels a few pips above 1.1400 during the European trading session.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness persists as BoJ hike talk grows – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny highlights persistent Japanese Yen weakness as USD/JPY trades at levels last seen in 1986, with low volatility undermining the Ministry of Finance’s case for intervention. He notes limited contagion in Japanese bonds but rising inflation and political pressure.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains strongly on hopes of BoJ aggressive tightening cycle
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) attracts significant bids against its major currency peers during the European trading session on Wednesday. The USD/JPY pair falls vertically to near 162.65, but quickly recovers some losses and rebounds to around 162.90.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Rate path hinges on inflation data – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke highlights recent confusion in Norway after delayed core inflation data and an unexpected slowdown in both headline and core rates.

item.title: Dow Jones futures slip as traders adopt caution on US-Iran tensions
item.description: Dow Jones futures lose 0.30% to trade around 52,290 during European trading hours on Wednesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.38% and 0.85%, trading near 7,520 and 29,070, respectively.

item.title: Euro retreats from one-month top amid JPY intervention risks, BoJ bets as traders eye ECB
item.description: The EUR/JPY cross attracts some sellers after an intraday move up to a one-month high and drops to the 185.75-185.70 area during the early part of the European session on Wednesday.
